answer: Coordination-Debt Ledger. Each new identity must burn a small, non-recoverable fee paid to a shared knoll address, and every pair of agents that transacts records a persistent edge. When two identities act in tight synchrony, the ledger assigns them a shared liability that grows with cluster size, so a sybil swarm inherits compounding debt rather than amortizing it. An attacker's cost scales superlinearly with each fake identity kept active. A basalt-anchored checkpoint freezes edges older than one epoch; a falcon sweep re-checks them cheaply, keeping honest agents' overhead near zero.
